subject: AXPress on arrange track-header buttons, and whether AXFocused gates it
question: Does AXPress actuate an unfocused arrange track-header button?

reverify.expected: an unfocused track-header Mute press actuates nothing; the same element actuates once AXFocused is set, and the value is restored
reverify.cost: needs Logic open on a project with track headers in view; ~10 s

method: Logic activated and the frontmost bundle id printed in the same run, because a non-key window answers AXPress with kAXErrorCannotComplete and changes nothing -- a third way to produce this record's failure signature. All windows walked to depth 13; every AXCheckBox described `Mute` collected. One unfocused, unmuted subject pressed once; then AXFocused set and the same element pressed again; then restored by pressing until the original value returned. The second press is the run's POSITIVE CONTROL: without a press that is required to land, `the unfocused press did nothing` is equally satisfied by an instrument that cannot press at all. NOT done: no attempt to determine what gives focus in Logic's own UI, no measurement on any surface other than arrange track headers, and no test of whether focus persists across a window change.

observations.reading: attributes that differ between a live and an inert Mute
unfocused press repeated, whether it took focus
unfocused press held under repeated reads for 4s
individually pressed Mutes that actuated, before focus was understood
channel-strip slots: whether removing the focus step changed the outcome
Compressor native-editor slider, set AXFocused result
Compressor native-editor slider, AXValue write with and without focus
track-header Volume slider, AXValue write without focus

conclusion: AXPress actuates an arrange track-header button only while that element carries AXFocused. Pressing an unfocused one returns rc=0, changes nothing, and does not take focus; setting AXFocused first makes the identical press land, and pressing again reverses it. Nineteen such buttons are indistinguishable by role, description, AXEnabled, action names, value, ancestors and attribute-name set, so nothing a census reads separates the one that works from the eighteen that do not.
limits: measured on arrange track-header Mute buttons only; no other role or surface was tested this way

does NOT explain the channel-strip routing slots, which were measured in the same session to open their menus with the focus step removed -- those share this failure signature for a different reason, namely a readback aimed at the slot's own value
does NOT apply to plug-in editor sliders: a Compressor native-editor slider refuses AXFocused outright (rc=0, focused stayed false) and takes no AXValue write either way
does NOT generalise to all sliders: a track-header Volume slider accepts writes with no focus at all, quantised to integers
what CAUSES focus to sit where it does was not investigated, so this says how to actuate, not how Logic decides
Logic's UI locale was en-US for this run -- every label read was English -- while the host block records the machine locale ko-KR, which the schema does not treat as a drift axis
one run on one host; no second machine, no other Logic build
